analysis.investment_thesis: Force Motors is a genuinely good business — ROCE of 30% and a spectacular debt-elimination story — but the stock is priced for perfection with an earnings yield of only ~3.8% (EBIT INR 1,099 Cr / EV ~INR 29,000 Cr), far below the Magic Formula's 12% threshold. The Magic Formula rule is simple: great business at the wrong price is still the wrong investment.
key_strengths: ROCE of 30% — clears the Magic Formula quality bar of 25%+ with room to spare
Debt effectively eliminated by FY25 (from INR 1,069 Cr in FY22 to just INR 17 Cr), massively improving capital structure
Operating leverage is real: revenue grew 2.5x from FY22→FY25 while EBITDA grew 11x (INR 101 Cr → INR 1,155 Cr)
key_risks: Earnings yield ~3.8% (EBIT/EV) is less than one-third of the 12% threshold — stock is expensive on any Magic Formula screen
Proven cyclicality: EBITDA cratered 76% (FY19→FY22) and net losses in FY21-FY22 show this is not a recession-resistant business
Other income spiked to INR 446 Cr in FY25 vs. INR 37 Cr in FY24 — inflates reported net profit of INR 801 Cr; core operating earnings are meaningfully lower
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~3.8% — stock must be avoided under Magic Formula rules regardless of business quality

Other income of INR 446 Cr (FY25) is nearly 56% of reported net profit — one-time or non-recurring items mask true earnings power; strip this out and core PAT is closer to ~INR 450–500 Cr, implying a P/E closer to 60x
P/E of 30.7x and EV/EBITDA of 20.25x leave no margin of safety for an auto manufacturer with demonstrated cyclicality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Force Motors yields a split verdict. On quality, it scores well: ROCE of 30% is excellent and the business has demonstrated real operating leverage — EBITDA expanded from INR 101 Cr (FY22) to INR 1,155 Cr (FY25) on a revenue base that grew only 2.5x, while simultaneously retiring over INR 1,050 Cr of debt. That is a legitimately impressive operational turnaround. However, the price reflects this turnaround fully. With EBIT of INR 1,099 Cr against an enterprise value of roughly INR 29,000 Cr (Market Cap INR 29,486 Cr + Debt INR 17 Cr − Cash INR 507 Cr), earnings yield is just ~3.8%. The Magic Formula requires both legs of the equation to work — here, only one does.

The FY25 profit quality also deserves scrutiny. Reported net profit of INR 801 Cr includes INR 446 Cr of "other income" (vs. INR 37 Cr in FY24) — the nature of this jump is unexplained in the data but likely includes asset sales or treasury gains. Strip it out at a 25% tax rate and core PAT falls to roughly INR 470 Cr, implying a P/E above 60x. This is a business I would love to own at half the price. At current valuations, the Mr. Market has already rewarded shareholders for the recovery — future returns will be ordinary at best.
